claims.text: Severe plastic deformation followed by annealing will improve the mechanical properties of FeNiCrMn high-entropy alloy.
The alloy is initially in the as-cast state.
The proposed intervention combines severe plastic deformation with subsequent annealing.
The processing is conducted at room temperature.
The processing is conducted at atmospheric pressure.
Severe plastic deformation followed by annealing refines the grains.
Severe plastic deformation followed by annealing precipitates secondary phases.
Grain refinement strengthens the alloy through grain-boundary strengthening.
Secondary-phase precipitation strengthens the alloy through precipitation hardening.
The proposed processing increases the yield strength relative to the as-cast alloy.
The proposed processing increases ductility relative to the as-cast alloy.
The relevant baseline is as-cast FeNiCrMn alloy without further processing.
Available data are insufficient to establish the effects of severe plastic deformation and annealing on the mechanical properties of FeNiCrMn alloy.

contradictions.description: The intervention includes annealing, but all processing conditions are stated to be at room temperature; conventional annealing requires an elevated temperature, and no distinct annealing temperature is provided.
